points: These are the cases that come up once a season.
A ball that bounces on your side and goes back over the net: you may reach over and play it, as long as you do not touch the net, the posts or their court.
A shot around the net post, even below net height, is legal if it lands in.
A ball that hits a scoring device or other object fixed to the net or post, and then lands in, loses the point.
You lose the point if you catch a ball before it bounces, or if it hits you, even when you stand outside the court.
You lose the point if you jump into their court, or if your racket flies out of your hand and lands there.
Rackets clashing in doubles is legal, unless both rackets clearly touched the ball.
A broken racket or string: finish the point with it. Then you may leave to get another one, for a reasonable time.

questions.q: Your opponent's drop shot bounces on your side and spins back over the net. Can you reach over the net to hit it?
options: Yes, if you do not touch the net, the posts or their court
No. You may never reach over the net
No. The point is theirs once the ball goes back
Yes, and touching the net is fine in this case
questions.why: You may reach over the net and play it back, as long as you do not touch the net, posts or their court.

questions.q: Pulled wide, you hit the ball around the net post, below the height of the net, and it lands in. What is the call?
options: You lose the point. The ball must go over the net
questions.why: A shot around the net post is legal. There is no requirement to clear the net.

questions.q: Singles on a court with a doubles net. During a point you touch the net post. What is the call?
options: You lose the point only if the net shook
questions.why: In singles played with a doubles net, the posts and the net outside the singles line are permanent fixtures, not the net for your match.

questions.q: Your shot hits the scoring device fixed to the net post and then drops into their court. What is the call?
options: Good, if it would have gone in anyway
questions.why: A scoring device or object attached to the net or post is a permanent fixture. If your ball hits it, you lose the point.

questions.q: Chasing a wide ball, you run past the net post and cross the line of the net, outside the post. You do not touch their court. What is the call?
options: Legal only if you hit the ball first
questions.why: Crossing the imaginary extension of the net, outside the post, is legal before or after hitting the ball, as long as you do not touch their court.

questions.q: To stop yourself after a drop shot, you jump over the net into their court while the ball is in play. What is the call?
options: Legal, if you did not touch the net
Legal, if you did not get in their way
questions.why: If you jump over the net into their court, you lose the point.

questions.q: Your racket flies out of your hand and lands in their court. It hits nobody. What is the call?
options: Play on, if nobody was hit
Their choice: replay or take the point
questions.why: If your racket flies out of your hand and lands in their court, you lose the point.

questions.q: You stand behind the baseline and catch a ball in the air that was clearly going out. What is the call?
options: Your point. The ball was going out
Your point, if you were outside the court
questions.why: If you catch a ball before it bounces, you lose the point, wherever you stand, inside or outside the court.

questions.q: You stand well outside the court. Their shot hits you before it bounces. What is the call?
options: Your point. The ball was going out
Your point, if you tried to get out of the way
questions.why: If the ball hits you, you lose the point. Standing outside the court does not help.

questions.q: Doubles. You and your partner both go for a ball and your rackets clash. Only one racket touched the ball. What is the call?
options: Legal only if the ball lands in the singles court
questions.why: Rackets clashing is legal, unless it is clear that both rackets touched the ball.

questions.q: Doubles. Your rackets clash and it is clear that both rackets touched the ball. What is the call?
options: Legal, if the ball lands in
questions.why: If it is clear that both rackets touched the ball, you lose the point.

questions.q: A string breaks in the middle of a rally. What do you do?
options: Finish the point with that racket, then you may get another one
Finish the game with that racket before you change
questions.why: Play on and finish the point with that racket. After the point you may leave the court to get another one, for a reasonable time.

questions.q: Your shoe breaks during a point. When may you leave the court to fix it?
options: After the point ends, for a reasonable time
At once. The point is replayed
Never. You play on or retire
questions.why: When clothing or a shoe breaks, you may leave the court after the point ends to fix it, for a reasonable time.
